name: Google Calendar
summary: Navigate Google Cloud projects, consent configuration, and Calendar permissions.

difficulty.explanation: Cloud configuration is straightforward; audience selection, least-privilege scopes, and production verification add decisions.

evidence.qualification: Editorial assessment of configuration decisions and permission complexity; not a provider rating.
Editorial estimate for registration and configuration with existing accounts and permissions. Excludes callback implementation, OAuth testing, policy preparation, and external review. Not measured.

approvalSummary.text: Public sensitive-scope access generally needs Google verification unless an exception applies. Registration alone is not verification.

approvalWaitingTime.text: Google says sensitive-scope verification can take up to 10 days. This is guidance for that review, not a guaranteed launch date or a total for other reviews.

prerequisites.text: A Google account with Calendar enabled and a Google Cloud project.
Permission to configure the project, plus an application name, support contact, and callback URL.

evidence.qualification: Preparation checklist inferred from the documented configuration steps; confirm project permissions with its owner.

steps.title: Enable Calendar API
steps.description: In your chosen Cloud project, enable the Google Calendar API.
steps.expectedOutcome: The API is enabled in that project.

steps.title: Configure consent and audience
steps.description: Open Google Auth Platform → Branding. Set app and contact details; select the appropriate Audience. Internal is for a Google Workspace organization; use External for outside users. In testing, add intended test users.
steps.expectedOutcome: Branding, audience, and test users match your intended access.

steps.title: Choose scopes
steps.description: In Data Access, select only the Calendar permissions your feature needs. Compare the examples below with the methods you will call.
steps.expectedOutcome: You have a least-privilege permission list.

steps.title: Create the web client
steps.description: Open Google Auth Platform → Clients → Create Client → Web application. Register the callback under authorized redirect URIs. Save the client ID and secret securely at creation; keep the secret off the frontend and out of source control.
steps.expectedOutcome: A web client exists with credentials stored privately.

steps.title: Use the correct callback setting
steps.description: For code exchange, redirect_uri must exactly match a registered callback, including path and port. Localhost HTTP is supported for local testing.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your callback and registered URI agree.

steps.title: Plan the authorization test
steps.description: In your own backend, use the official library to request selected scopes with state at https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth (response_type=code). Validate returned state and exchange the code at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token. Request offline access only if background access is needed. Then call events.list on a test calendar.
steps.expectedOutcome: Expected: consent, a valid token response, and an authorized API result. This has not been performed here.

steps.title: Do not mix browser and server examples
steps.description: The JavaScript quickstart uses browser client configuration, authorized JavaScript origins, and an API key. An origin identifies a browser site; it is not a callback path. Follow the web-server guide for the primary flow here.
steps.expectedOutcome: You have kept browser-origin configuration separate from your server callback.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly
scopes.purpose: Read events on calendars you can access. Candidate for an event viewer.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events
scopes.purpose: View and edit events. Request only when the feature needs event changes.

approval.text: Check sensitive/restricted scope classifications and verification exceptions before public release. A Calendar read scope can still be sensitive.
For sensitive-scope review, prepare domain ownership, policy information, scope justification, and a demonstration video. Submit through Verification Center.
Workspace administrators may independently restrict sensitive-scope access.

blockers.action: Correct the callback URI in the client configuration or authorization request so they match exactly.
Check External audience test users and confirm that an Internal app is not being used by an outside account.
Review the app’s scope classifications, exceptions, and verification path before broader release. Do not treat client creation as approval.

agent.text: Compare Calendar methods with candidate scopes and draft a registration checklist.

evidence.qualification: Suggested division of work, not a provider rule or a claim that an agent has performed these actions.

developer.text: Own the Cloud project; enter credentials into a private backend configuration, approve consent, and submit any required verification.

evidence.qualification: Suggested division of work, not a provider rule or a claim that an agent has performed these actions.

nextActions.text: Choose a read-only or write feature and record its exact callback URL.

evidence.qualification: Suggested division of work, not a provider rule or a claim that an agent has performed these actions.

nextActions.text: Implement and test the callback separately, then assess production verification for your chosen audience.

evidence.qualification: Suggested division of work, not a provider rule or a claim that an agent has performed these actions.

nextActions.text: For a read-only smoke test, call GET https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/primary/events with the authorized user’s access token. An empty event list can still be a successful response.

evidence.qualification: Suggested test based on the documented events.list endpoint. Run only in your own application; this navigator has not executed it.

name: Slack
summary: Understand app registration, bot scopes, workspace installation, and distribution.

difficulty.explanation: The main decisions are bot versus user access, callback configuration, and workspace or distribution restrictions.

evidence.qualification: Editorial assessment of configuration decisions and permission complexity; not a provider rating.
Editorial estimate for registration and configuration with existing accounts and permissions. Excludes callback implementation, OAuth testing, policy preparation, and external review. Not measured.

sources.title: Create an app from app settings

approvalSummary.text: Workspace installation permission and Marketplace review are separate. Commercial distribution should go through Marketplace submission and approval.

evidence.qualification: The inspected sources do not establish a review or workspace approval duration for your app.

prerequisites.text: A Slack workspace where you can install apps; an Admin or Owner may need to grant permission.
A defined app use case and a chosen HTTPS callback URL for your own backend. Callback implementation is separate from app registration.

evidence.qualification: Preparation inferred from Slack’s scope and redirect requirements; implementing or hosting a callback is outside the setup estimate.

steps.title: Create your Slack app
steps.description: In Slack’s app dashboard, choose Blank app → Continue. Enter the App Name, select the development Workspace, then select Create.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Slack app exists in the selected development workspace.

steps.title: Save client credentials
steps.description: In the app settings, open Basic Information → App Credentials. Locate the Client ID and Client Secret; store them privately for your backend.
steps.expectedOutcome: The backend can reference this app’s credentials without committing them to source control.

steps.title: Register the HTTPS callback
steps.description: Open OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs. Add your backend’s HTTPS callback and save it. When redirect_uri is sent at authorization, send that same value at token exchange.
steps.expectedOutcome: The callback is registered and the authorization and exchange requests agree on its URI.

steps.title: Select bot or user permissions
steps.description: Open OAuth & Permissions → Scopes. Add the minimum Bot Token Scopes for the feature; choose User Token Scopes only for actions on behalf of a user.
steps.expectedOutcome: The configured scopes match the intended bot or user action.

steps.title: Authorize from your own app
steps.description: In your application, direct the user to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with client_id, scope for bot access or user_scope for user access, redirect_uri, and state. Validate state at the backend callback.
steps.expectedOutcome: After consent, the callback receives an authorization code.

steps.title: Exchange and test separately
steps.description: Your backend posts the code and client credentials to https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access. Check ok and any error before using tokens. Use a permitted test action in your development workspace.
steps.expectedOutcome: A successful exchange returns ok: true and an installation token. Check the permitted action separately; no OAuth test was run here.

steps.title: Review distribution
steps.description: For other workspaces, review Manage Distribution. Unlisted distribution supports pilots; apps intended for commercial distribution should be submitted and approved for Marketplace listing.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your intended distribution path is identified.

scopes.name: chat:write
scopes.purpose: Send messages as the app. It does not by itself allow posting in every public channel.

scopes.name: channels:read
scopes.purpose: Example bot permission to access public-channel information, not message history.

scopes.name: scope vs. user_scope
scopes.purpose: Bot scopes use scope; user scopes use user_scope. Keep Sign in with Slack scopes in a separate OAuth flow from ordinary app scopes.

approval.text: Ask your workspace Admin or Owner if installation is restricted.
Installing in a development workspace does not establish approval for wider distribution. Marketplace apps undergo review.

blockers.action: Use the same redirect_uri in the authorization request and token exchange. Confirm the saved HTTPS Redirect URL.
Check the credentials against App Credentials for the same Slack app.
Restart authorization for a new code rather than retrying an invalid value.

evidence.qualification: Recovery recommendation based on the documented invalid-code error; verify callback handling if it repeats.

blockers.issue: Bot cannot post in a channel
blockers.action: Check chat:write and channel membership. Invite the app to the channel, or assess whether chat:write.public is truly needed.

agent.text: Draft scope comparisons, callback implementation notes, and a distribution checklist.

evidence.qualification: Suggested division of work, not a provider rule or a claim that an agent has performed these actions.

developer.text: Create and own the app, protect credentials, obtain administrator consent, and test installation in the intended workspace.

evidence.qualification: Suggested division of work, not a provider rule or a claim that an agent has performed these actions.

name: Notion
summary: Plan a public connection, its capabilities, and access to selected workspace content.

difficulty.explanation: Public OAuth requires choosing an installation scope, capabilities, and content access as well as configuring the callback.

evidence.qualification: Editorial assessment of configuration decisions and permission complexity; not a provider rating.
Editorial estimate for registration and configuration with existing accounts and permissions. Excludes callback implementation, OAuth testing, policy preparation, and external review. Not measured.

sources.title: Create a token and redirect URI rules

approvalSummary.text: Marketplace listing is optional and separate from public OAuth. Listing submissions are reviewed; only Any workspace public connections are eligible.

approvalWaitingTime.text: For Marketplace submissions, Notion says to expect an email response within 5–10 business days. This is a response expectation, not guaranteed approval or a prerequisite wait for ordinary OAuth.

prerequisites.text: A Notion account with access to the Developer portal and a workspace for testing the public connection.
Access to pages you can share: the OAuth page picker shows resources where the authorizing user has full access.
A chosen installation scope and backend callback URL. These are inputs to registration; you do not need an existing OAuth connection to begin.

evidence.qualification: Preparation checklist inferred from public-connection configuration; verify any organization-specific permissions with an administrator.

steps.title: Create your Notion OAuth connection
steps.description: In the Notion Developer portal, open Build → Connections → Create new connection. Enter the connection name and development workspace, and choose the installation scope: Any workspace for a public integration, or specific workspaces for a scoped OAuth integration.
steps.expectedOutcome: A connection is created with the intended installation scope; that scope cannot be changed afterward.

steps.title: Configure capabilities
steps.description: In the connection’s Developer portal settings, select the content and user capabilities needed by the feature. For a read-only exporter, review Read content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The connection requests the capabilities needed for the intended operations.

steps.title: Configure OAuth and credentials
steps.description: In the connection’s OAuth configuration, register redirect URI(s). Open Configuration to retrieve the client ID and secret; keep the secret out of source control and frontend code.
steps.expectedOutcome: The backend callback is registered and the credentials are stored privately.

steps.title: Start authorization and select pages
steps.description: From the portal’s Configuration tab, use the authorization URL in your own application with a state value. The user reviews capabilities and selects pages before consent.
steps.expectedOutcome: The callback receives a code after consent, or an error if access is denied.

steps.title: Exchange the code on your backend
steps.description: POST JSON to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token with grant_type: authorization_code and code. Use HTTP Basic authentication with base64(client_id:client_secret). Include redirect_uri when it was supplied at authorization or multiple URIs exist; omit it for a single configured URI when absent from authorization.
steps.expectedOutcome: A successful token response is available to your backend. Handle errors and keep credentials private.

steps.title: Run a separate content-access test
steps.description: In your own implementation, correlate the returned state, handle cancellation, and try a permitted read on selected content. Compare a denied or unshared resource too.
steps.expectedOutcome: Selected content is accessible only as permitted. These checks have not been run here.

evidence.qualification: Suggested test procedure inferred from documented page access and OAuth behavior; use your own backend.

steps.title: Consider Marketplace only if needed
steps.description: For optional listing, use Listings → Connections, prepare listing details, and submit for review.
steps.expectedOutcome: A listing submission is distinct from OAuth setup.

scopes.name: Read content
scopes.purpose: Read existing content; it does not grant write access.

scopes.name: Insert content / Update content
scopes.purpose: Insert creates content; Update changes existing content. Neither automatically grants all other capabilities.

scopes.name: Installation scope and page access
scopes.purpose: Installation scope controls eligible workspaces. Page selection controls content access; capabilities control operations. These are not Google-style scope URI strings.

approval.text: Public OAuth can be used without a Marketplace listing. A listing is an optional review process.
Selected workspaces only connections are not Marketplace-eligible; create a new connection if a different installation scope is needed.
OAuth authorization can start once client credentials and the redirect URI are configured; Marketplace submission or review is not required.

blockers.action: Treat cancellation as a declined request; offer the user a deliberate way to restart authorization.
Apply the token endpoint’s conditional redirect_uri rule; do not always include or always omit it.
Check capabilities and whether the resource was shared with the connection; inspect the error code and message.
Have the user re-authenticate after changing public-connection capabilities.

agent.text: Compare content operations with capabilities and draft a callback and page-access test checklist.

evidence.qualification: Suggested division of work, not a provider rule or a claim that an agent has performed these actions.

developer.text: Own the connection, choose installation scope, handle secrets, authorize selected pages, and perform the real OAuth test.

evidence.qualification: Suggested division of work, not a provider rule or a claim that an agent has performed these actions.

nextActions.text: Choose the installation scope carefully before registering the connection.

evidence.qualification: Suggested division of work, not a provider rule or a claim that an agent has performed these actions.
